text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past purchases as broad, continuing interests more reliably than as evidence of a specific next need.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Direct continuations of repeated interests, including familiar artists, related albums and recurring supplies, often give users a clear reason to choose.",
    "Complementary items appeal when they support existing equipment, extend a demonstrated activity or add a useful capability."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products compete with closer matches despite requiring an unsupported project, device or listening preference.",
    "Recommendations repeat recently satisfied needs or revive older interests without adequately reflecting how recent purchases change the next likely choice.",
    "Related accessories and supplies are treated as plausible choices before their compatibility, dimensions, capacity or quantity fit is established."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, brand, ecosystem, genre and era associations substitute for a specific connection to the user's purpose.",
    "Popularity, familiar names and shared product features appear to receive more weight than their ability to satisfy a demonstrated current need."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent sequences distinguish useful next steps from redundant purchases and older interests that may no longer be active.",
    "Specific functional and musical connections matter more than broad resemblance: compatible support, practical task fit, familiar vocals, melody and mood.",
    "Users distinguish a generally appealing item from one compelling enough to choose now, and often want only one item serving a particular role."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Broadly plausible associations occupy top positions without enough evidence of a specific, timely reason to choose, crowding out useful complements and closer continuations of recent intent.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of assessable top-ranked recommendations users would choose now, distinguished from items they merely consider relevant.",
    "The frequency of rejections attributed to unsupported needs, incompatible specifications or duplication of recently satisfied needs.",
    "The relative rank and acceptance of direct continuations and useful complements compared with broad category, brand or popularity matches.",
    "The frequency of unassessable recommendations, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
